summary: Draft Control Power record. `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests` sits under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power`, has an explicit repo-doc default of `1`, is absent on the observed clean baseline, produced an exact current-build Unicode string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and was later retained by source-enrichment as a docs-first kernel candidate with a `power-request-simulation` trigger recommendation. A later repo-native follow-up then exposed that same trigger family as a named guest Procmon profile and mega-trigger runtime alias. A later KVM local-KD pass then resolved live current-build `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1`, which aligns with the repo-doc default. A later current-build disassembly pass then showed direct consumers in `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate` and `nt!PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired`. Later follow-ups then showed `nt!PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery` packaging requester state for `nt!PopUmpoSendPowerMessage`, `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` staying timeout-setting specific by updating `nt!PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, the timeout timer/worker chain feeding back into `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`, and the broader override-response plus callback-worker path staying queue and PDC driven with no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbol. The lane is strong enough for a schema-backed draft, but still lacks a registry seeding path and an exact runtime registry read.

setting.name: Allow System Required Power Requests
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a kernel-adjacent Control Power setting tied to how the power manager treats system-required power requests. It is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel and power researchers may inspect this value when investigating how system-required power requests are converted, honored, or suppressed under undocumented power-policy flows.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value now has a stronger evidence chain because it has repo docs, observed baseline state, an exact current-build string hit, a retained enrichment recommendation, a repo-native trigger harness, a live current-build KVM local-KD value that matches the repo-doc default, direct current-build consumer disassembly, a visible UMPO override-query lineage, a timeout-setting callback disassembly, a retained timeout timer/worker chain, and a retained override-response plus callback-worker follow-up that still exposed no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbol. It is still too weak for a published tweak because no current-build registry seeding path has been demonstrated and an exact runtime registry read remains unresolved.
setting.professional_notes: Repo power docs assign `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests = 1` under `Control\\Power` and map it to `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`. The power routing note later kept the value inside the `Control\\Power` docs cluster. The observed clean baseline then confirmed that the parent `Control\\Power` path exists while the value itself is absent. A later targeted current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests` in `ntoskrnl.exe`, which is stronger than a pure docs-only mention and enough to keep the value out of raw backlog. Source-enrichment later retained the candidate in the canonical queue with `power-request-simulation` as the suggested trigger family, specifically `PowerCreateRequest(SystemRequired)`, `PowerSetRequest(DisplayRequired)`, and an audio playback session. A later repo-native follow-up then exposed that same trigger family as a named guest Procmon profile plus a matching mega-trigger runtime alias, closing the old trigger-design gap before the first dedicated narrow replay. A later KVM local-KD pass then resolved live current-build `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1`, which matches the repo-doc default and also surfaced the sibling symbol `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired` in the same wildcard sweep. A later current-build disassembly pass then showed direct reads of `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution` inside `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate` and `nt!PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired`, while `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` chained into that same reader family through `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionmentUpdate`. A later wildcard lineage pass then showed that the current build exposes only one `*PowerRequest*Setting*` symbol, `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`, alongside `PopPowerRequestInitialize`, `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize`, and the `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` family. A later init/override disassembly pass then showed `PopPowerRequestInitialize` only zeroing per-object fields and `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize` iterating `PopPowerRequestObjectList` before calling `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery`, which is useful because it still did not expose a registry read in the visible current-build init path. A later dedicated UMPO disassembly pass then showed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery` storing requester identity via `PoStoreRequester`, allocating an `Umpo`-tagged buffer, and dispatching `PopUmpoSendPowerMessage`, while wildcard output exposed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestCreate`, `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestAction`, and `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideCleanup`. A later dedicated callback disassembly pass then showed `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` comparing the incoming GUID against `GUID_EXECUTION_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, requiring a 4-byte payload, writing `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, rearming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer`, and then calling `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. A later timeout-lineage pass then showed `PopPowerRequestSetExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` reading `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, comparing it against `PopExecutionRequiredContext`, and arming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` via `KeSetTimer2`, while `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutCallback` simply queued work and `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutWorker` re-entered `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. A later response-lineage follow-up then showed `x nt!*PowerRequest*Reg*` returning no visible current-build symbols, `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestOverrideQueryResponse` updating request state, re-evaluating pending request status, and queueing `PopPowerRequestUpdateWorkItem`, `PopPowerRequestCallbackWorker` draining the update queue through `PopPowerRequestStatsSetActive` and `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestUpdate`, and `PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired` consulting `PoPdcCallbacks`, updating `PopPowerRequestPdcNotifiedExecutionRequired` or `PopPowerRequestPdcNotifiedSystemRequired`, testing `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`, and then writing `PopSIdle` policy state before `PopCheckResiliencyScenarios`. This matters because the visible family is now callback/init/timeout-setting/timer-worker/UMPO/override-response/PDC driven and still does not demonstrate a registry read or a direct write to `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`. The next proof step is no longer a generic reader hunt; it is whether any registry seeding path exists outside this visible family on modern builds.

evidence.title: Source-enrichment keeps AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests as a docs-first kernel candidate with a power-request trigger family

evidence.title: KVM local-KD resolves live PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD pass resolved `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution` and read its live value as `1`. The same wildcard sweep also resolved the sibling symbol `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired`, but did not read its value.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows current-build consumers for PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD disassembly pass showed direct reads of `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution` in `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate` and `nt!PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired`. The same pass also showed `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` chaining into `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionmentUpdate`.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD wildcard pass narrows execution-required setting lineage
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD wildcard pass showed that the current build exposes only one `*PowerRequest*Setting*` symbol, `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`, alongside `PopPowerRequestInitialize`, `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize`, and the `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` family. This narrows the visible lineage to callback/init surfaces rather than a demonstrated registry reader.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows init and override path without a visible registry read
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD disassembly pass showed `PopPowerRequestInitialize` only zeroing per-object fields, while `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize` iterated `PopPowerRequestObjectList` and called `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery`. The visible init/override path did not expose a registry read.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows UMPO override-query lineage without a visible registry read
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD follow-up showed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery` calling `PoStoreRequester`, allocating an `Umpo`-tagged buffer, and dispatching `PopUmpoSendPowerMessage`. The same wildcard pass exposed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestCreate`, `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestAction`, and `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideCleanup`, keeping the visible lineage callback/init/UMPO-query centric rather than registry-backed.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows timeout-setting callback semantics for the execution-required family
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD pass showed `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` matching `GUID_EXECUTION_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, requiring a 4-byte payload, writing `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, rearming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer`, and then calling `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. The visible callback is timeout-setting specific rather than a demonstrated registry-backed seeding path for `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows execution-required timeout timer and worker lineage
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD pass showed `PopPowerRequestSetExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` reading `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` and arming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` through `KeSetTimer2`, `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutCallback` queueing work with `PopQueueWorkItem`, and `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutWorker` re-entering `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. The visible timeout family remains runtime timer/worker driven rather than registry-backed.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows execution-required override-response and callback-worker lineage
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD follow-up showed `x nt!*PowerRequest*Reg*` returning no visible current-build symbols, `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestOverrideQueryResponse` updating request state and queueing `PopPowerRequestUpdateWorkItem`, `PopPowerRequestCallbackWorker` draining the update queue through `PopPowerRequestStatsSetActive` and `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestUpdate`, and `PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired` consulting `PoPdcCallbacks`, `PopPowerRequestPdcNotified*`, `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`, and `PopSIdle`. The visible family remained runtime callback and queue driven rather than registry-backed.

decision.why: The candidate is strong enough for a schema-backed draft because it has a repo-doc default, observed baseline state, a current-build string hit, a retained enrichment recommendation, a matching repo-native trigger harness, a live KVM local-KD value that aligns with the repo-doc default, direct current-build callback/reader disassembly, a visible UMPO override-query lineage, a timeout-setting callback disassembly, a retained timeout timer/worker chain, and a retained override-response plus callback-worker follow-up that still exposed no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbol. It is not ready for validation because no current-build registry seeding path has been demonstrated and an exact runtime registry read remains unresolved.

open_questions: Does any current-build path still seed `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests` from `Control\\Power`, or is the visible callback/init/timeout-setting/timer-worker/UMPO/override-response/PDC family registry-free on modern builds?
